title: Large personal Amiga/DOS game resources and tracker-format discovery
summary: Personally screen 477 candidate URLs and add 15 projects, with nine explicit non-promotion decisions.
notes: Root personally searched 12 GitHub query routes, screened 477 unique URLs and inspected 24 pinned repository trees. Fifteen additions and nine explicit non-promotions. Game resource recovery, native source-derived ports, original binary repair and tracker-format compatibility are distinguished from runtime emulation, new tools and source-platform mismatches. No upstream program, compiler, game, converter, emulator or service was executed.

sources.reason: Original-address-backed repair toolkit fixes table accesses, object slot leakage, sample names and other original DOS behavior. Inspected expected-byte-guarded patches and rebuild setup, not merely launch settings.
Reads original DAT image/sound archives and map data in C#/SFML reconstruction. Inspected DAT 16-bit length/32-bit offset reader.
Historical Unity implementation of Underworld resources, object systems and conversation language. Inspected actual conversation VM opcodes, not x86 CPU emulation.
Recovers original tile meshes, map placement/height, image and sprite descriptors with browser viewer/OBJ export. Inspected map assembly and mesh rotation logic backed by format specifications.
Repository contains Stunts Stressed resource editor and Midtown Madness 3 format tools/specifications. Inspected Stunts shape/resource model and supported-format boundaries.
Analyzes original level-six out-of-bounds behavior and implements level/warp-zone parsing and editing with exact executable offsets. Inspected special-level and initial-state mappings.
C99 library/C++ CLI for original sprite, pitch, palette, planar and script formats. Inspected 24-byte DOS sprite record decoding and bit-carry codec translation.
Original C# graphics toolkit decodes/rebuilds SWOS pitch maps, bitplanes and palettes, with Tiled interoperability. Inspected 42-by-55 pitch mapping and planar constants.
Reconstructs 78 regions from a fingerprinted original ADF for native tennis engine. Inspected extractor and deterministic integer ball arc/range implementation.

MMD0–MMD3 converter recovers MIDI timing, hold/velocity behavior and SysEx layouts using original hardware/interpreter measurements. Inspected note-start/hold implementation and original routine references.
Parses and writes historical .info icon structures alongside PNG conversion and palette reduction. Inspected native icon reader/writer implementation.
Parses original instruments, patterns and effects into RCM for a replacement Amiga replay routine. Inspected ProTracker module header/instrument reader.
Independent native parsing/sequencing/mixing for MOD/S3M/XM/IT, plus narrower browser MOD implementation. Inspected MOD layout validation and FLT8 paired-pattern handling.
SDLPoP-derived native ARM64 game with new bounded save codec and macOS/Metal integration. Inspected explicit world/audio snapshot serialization and validation.
Ports established recovered SDLPoP engine to Dreamcast. Inspected original-address-annotated native level loop and state initialization.

Inspected main loop never advances the decoder because fc.run is commented out, and prints diagnostics rather than writing Standard MIDI. Bundled decoder is substantive prior work but the advertised converter is not established as usable.
Amiga A520 replacement video hardware, not game/application source or format reconstruction.

BBC Micro-origin engine targeting Amiga, with generated native and CPU sources retained. Amiga target alone does not make it an Amiga-origin reconstruction for this focused pass; do not claim independent semantic port from the README.
Native STE source port of modern Atari 8-bit Flob. Source platform is Atari 8-bit, not one of the requested four; retain as a cross-platform lead.

Modern board-game rules reconstruction inspired by rediscovered Pascal printout, with selectable altered rules. Current repository does not establish a recovered DOS source implementation; original Tripppin is already tracked.
New automatic save/config backup utility for MiSTer VHD games, not recovery of a historical application or game format.
Native-feeling SDL/libretro wrapper and packaging framework, not recovered game logic. Hiding emulator UI does not make a native reconstruction.
AmiLisp/CL-Amiga implementation is already tracked under mdbergmann/cl-amiga. Current README identifies earlier Clamiga name; do not create a second project for rebranding.
New Z80 assembler/linker and CPC tooling, not a restored historical game/application. Useful development tooling but outside this subject-focused discovery batch.
